entry.title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving High-Dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR In the AI era, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on vector databases is critical as it supports similarity retrieval over high-dimensional vectors, which is essential for many large language model (LLM)…

In the AI era, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on vector databases is critical as it supports similarity retrieval over high-dimensional vectors, which is essential for many large language model (LLM) applications. To reduce costs and improve scalability, vector databases are often outsourced to cloud servers, raising privacy concerns for users whose query vectors contain sensitive information. In this work, we study the problem of asymmetric privacy-preserving ANN search, where the vector database is public but user queries must remain private from an untrusted cloud server.

  • To reduce costs and improve scalability, vector databases are often outsourced to cloud servers, raising privacy concerns for users whose query vectors contain sensitive information.
  • To solve this problem, we propose ObliSC, an efficient privacy-preserving search framework that protects query privacy against access-pattern leakage.

Datasets: ANN, Across

entry.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search.

Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $α$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{α+1}{α-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $γ> 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}γ$ approximation on navigable graphs ($α\approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees.

  • Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall.

Datasets: Big-ANN

entry.title: Standardized Tolerance for Adaptive Reuse and Repair: A Method for HNSW Migration Under Embedding Model Change Scenarios
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR When an embedding model changes, the same collection is re-encoded, and its vector index must be adapted to the new embedding space.

When an embedding model changes, the same collection is re-encoded, and its vector index must be adapted to the new embedding space. Because the source and target vectors represent the same objects, suitable connections in the source index can be reused. We propose STARR (Standardized Tolerance for Adaptive Reuse and Repair) to migrate HNSW indexes after an embedding model change.

  • We propose STARR (Standardized Tolerance for Adaptive Reuse and Repair) to migrate HNSW indexes after an embedding model change.

entry.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed retrieval budgets.

Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed retrieval budgets. However, optimizing distribution diversity or target-level interest separation ignores set-level retrieval geometry: sampled queries collapse onto overlapping ANN neighborhoods, while discrete top-K lookup and single-target supervision block end-to-end coverage optimization. We introduce CACO (Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization), a lightweight self-supervised post-training framework that coordinates queries from frozen flow-matching and diffusion retrievers toward complementary item coverage with negligible additional inference latency.

  • We introduce CACO (Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization), a lightweight self-supervised post-training framework that coordinates queries from frozen flow-matching and diffusion retrievers toward complementary item coverage with negligible additional…
  • CACO uses empirical retrieval frequencies across sampled reference queries as a relevance proxy, formulating a label-free coverage objective that improves recall across all 30 backbone-dataset settings in offline greedy selection experiments.
  • On eight public benchmarks and an in-house 24-partition streaming industrial dataset, CACO improves Recall@100 by up to 23.7% and Recall@400 by up to 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by 53.3%-64.9%, and adds only 0.5%-3.0% inference…

Datasets: Amazon Reviews

entry.title: Revocation Window in RAG: Quantifying Unauthorized Retrieval Exposure During Access-Control Propagation
entry.content:
[PP] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

TL;DR Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often store document chunks in a vector index together with a copy of their access-control metadata.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often store document chunks in a vector index together with a copy of their access-control metadata. When a user's permission is revoked in the authoritative permission store, this indexed copy may remain stale, allowing the vector database to keep returning protected content. This paper measures the duration of this revocation window and separates two outcomes: unauthorized index retrieval, in which the vector database returns a protected chunk, and LLM-context exposure, in which that chunk reaches the context assembled for the language model.

  • Query-time and hybrid authorization blocked protected content at the first post-revocation probe (0 ms at probe resolution) even though the stale index kept returning it, while the no-worker control never achieved stable enforcement within the window.

Datasets: n/a

entry.title: Exploring Semantic Table Search in Data Lakes
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Discovery of relevant datasets within data lakes remains a key challenge.

Discovery of relevant datasets within data lakes remains a key challenge. Union and join search are effective techniques for discovering data when augmenting an existing table. In exploratory search, instead, keyword search is commonly adopted to find a relatively small set of highly relevant tables matching some search terms.

  • In this work, we propose \texttt{Thetis++}, which combines keyword and semantic table search to discover relevant tables that combine the semantic signal with the presence of exact keyword matches.
  • Furthermore, while indexes for keyword search are quite efficient, here we provide insights into how to improve the scalability of prefiltering techniques for semantic search, comparing LSH indexes with Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds.
  • Our experiments show that HNSW drastically improves the runtime of semantic table search by 4.7X on average whilst retaining the high-quality tables.

entry.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes.

Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes. This work introduces a method for visualizing and measuring ANN decision boundary geometry directly in the high-dimensional input space, avoiding distortions found with traditional projection-based techniques. We analyze boundary curvatures and distances in diverse inputs, architectures, and training methods.

  • Training methodology has a significantly stronger impact on boundary distance and curvature than architecture or test-set accuracy.
  • Our analytically and empirically supported methodology lays the foundation for future studies to improve network interpretability and understanding.

entry.title: SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query
entry.content:
[T1] ICDE 2027

TL;DR Multi-vector retrieval models such as ColBERT achieve state-of-the-art effectiveness by representing documents as sets of token-level vectors and scoring via MaxSim, but their high computational cost limits scalability…

Multi-vector retrieval models such as ColBERT achieve state-of-the-art effectiveness by representing documents as sets of token-level vectors and scoring via MaxSim, but their high computational cost limits scalability to large corpora. Existing approximate methods face fundamental bottlenecks: centroid interaction matrix approaches require computing a full matrix at every query and rely on GPU-accelerated clustering, while data-oblivious compression methods yield unstable recall that requires repeated compensation. We propose SIMQ (Single graph Index for Multi-vector Query), a framework that bridges single-vector graph indices and multi-vector retrieval through data-aware sampling-based clustering and per-token graph navigation, simultaneously bypassing all aforementioned bottlenecks.

  • We propose SIMQ (Single graph Index for Multi-vector Query), a framework that bridges single-vector graph indices and multi-vector retrieval through data-aware sampling-based clustering and per-token graph navigation, simultaneously bypassing all…
  • Building on this foundation, SIMQ+ further introduces count-based scoring and a dynamic candidate set to improve robustness across varying query conditions.

entry.title: Errpedia: Is Your Exact $k$-NN Vector Search Really Exact?
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Exact $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) vector search is a common feature of vector libraries and database systems.

Exact $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) vector search is a common feature of vector libraries and database systems. It serves applications that require exact results and provides the ground truth for evaluating approximate search. However, floating-point rounding and overflow can cause an exact search to return mathematically incorrect top-$k$ result sets.

  • We present Errpedia, a purpose-built dataset for testing the numerical correctness of exact vector search.
  • We release Errpedia as a reproducible benchmark for developers and researchers to test their implementations.

entry.title: Pelorus: Warped-Product Graph Indexing for Hyperbolic Vector Search
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Hyperbolic embeddings capture hierarchical relations, but million-scale approximate nearest neighbor search must reconcile geodesic fidelity with memory efficiency.

Hyperbolic embeddings capture hierarchical relations, but million-scale approximate nearest neighbor search must reconcile geodesic fidelity with memory efficiency. Flat inner-product indices distort order across radial shells, while native hyperbolic graphs repeatedly access full-precision vectors or quantize coordinates with singular conformal scales. We present Pelorus, a warped-product proximity-graph index for hyperbolic vector search.

  • We present Pelorus, a warped-product proximity-graph index for hyperbolic vector search.
  • At 99% Recall@10, it improves Cohere-1M throughput by 4.30x on one thread and 6.31x on 24 threads, and delivers 53,483 QPS on MERU-1M.

Datasets: ImageNet, Hyperbolic

entry.title: UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval
entry.content:
[T1] ICDE 2027

TL;DR Hybrid dense-sparse vector retrieval combines semantic signals from dense representations with lexical signals from sparse representations, typically ranking items by a query-dependent weighted sum of dense and sparse…

Hybrid dense-sparse vector retrieval combines semantic signals from dense representations with lexical signals from sparse representations, typically ranking items by a query-dependent weighted sum of dense and sparse vector distances. Existing systems commonly search separate dense and sparse vector indexes and rerank the union of their candidates, incurring two retrieval passes and potentially discarding items that rank highly only after the semantic and lexical signals are combined. Constructing a graph-based index directly under a hybrid distance can mitigate this premature candidate loss.

  • Therefore, we propose a Unified Hybrid Graph (UniGraph), which merges neighbor sets computed at multiple hybrid weights into a single bounded-degree graph index, enabling hybrid vector retrieval with different query-specific weights without index…
  • We further develop an adaptive weight-guided search framework that chooses between sparse- and dense-guided entry points according to the query weight, together with a dense-first hybrid distance pruning strategy that avoids unnecessary exact sparse distance…

Datasets: HotpotQA, BEIR

entry.title: HorizANN: Elastically Scaling Vector Search with Ghost Edges
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is fundamental to modern data-intensive AI applications such as retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation systems, and semantic search.

Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is fundamental to modern data-intensive AI applications such as retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation systems, and semantic search. Among existing indexing methods, graph-based indexes emerge as the state of the art due to their superior recall-throughput tradeoffs. Scaling these indexes to multiple machines requires partitioning the data and building indexes on each.

  • In this work, we present HorizANN, a distributed graph-based ANNS system that scales horizontally without requiring full index reconstruction.
  • To achieve this, we introduce ghost edges, a mechanism for preserving cross-partition connectivity as partition boundaries change during repartitioning.

entry.title: Leveraging Binary Hashing for Scalable Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index…

Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index assignment. This paper inves- tigates binary hashing techniques from the information retrieval literature as semantic indexing strategies for general-purpose networks. We study random Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) along with Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-, Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA)-, and ITQ (Iterative Quantization)- based variants in a semantic communication pipeline over a Binary Symmetric Channel.

  • Ex- periments on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) and the Banking77 dataset show that data-dependent hashing improves upon random LSH, while ITQ refinement increases robustness to channel noise.

Datasets: Banking77, All

entry.title: CARE: Contrastive-Anchored Residual Encoding with Listwise Reconstruction for Retrieval-Oriented Semantic IDs
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with the generation of a document's semantic ID (SID), so the SID tokenizer bounds what the retriever can recall.

Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with the generation of a document's semantic ID (SID), so the SID tokenizer bounds what the retriever can recall. Common SID constructions (residual k-means, RQ-VAE, finite scalar quantization, capacity balancing) optimize criteria defined on document embeddings alone and do not control whether a query can still find its relevant documents after quantization. We propose two retrieval-oriented SID tokenizers.

  • We propose two retrieval-oriented SID tokenizers.
  • In offline evaluation on industrial video search data, both tokenizers achieve higher reconstruction-view recall than residual k-means, and CARE-LR improves further on CARE-SID, mainly through the listwise distillation.

entry.title: When the Bill Falls: Reusing the Old Index Defers,Never Avoids, Re-encoding in Complete Embedding-Model Migration
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Upgrading the embedding model behind a vector index requires re-encoding the corpus.

Upgrading the embedding model behind a vector index requires re-encoding the corpus. Recent work reuses the old index through adapters or window re-ranking. Across sixteen model pairs on passage and code corpora, plus eleven on Natural Questions (NQ), we find three results.

  • Across sixteen model pairs on passage and code corpora, plus eleven on Natural Questions (NQ), we find three results.
  • First, reuse never avoids re-encoding: if migration must complete, every strategy eventually encodes every document; reuse only changes when that work is paid and the quality served meanwhile.

entry.title: CapCover Filter: Semantic Approximate Membership Queries over Embeddings
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Determining whether an embedding is sufficiently similar to any vector in a vector store without performing a nearest-neighbor search can substantially improve query throughput in vector-store systems.

Determining whether an embedding is sufficiently similar to any vector in a vector store without performing a nearest-neighbor search can substantially improve query throughput in vector-store systems. We study Semantic Approximate Membership Queries (SAMQs), which allow queries to be rejected when no indexed vector meets the requested similarity threshold, while guaranteeing no false negatives. We introduce CapCover Filter, a geometric data structure that summarizes a set of embeddings using spherical caps.

  • We introduce CapCover Filter, a geometric data structure that summarizes a set of embeddings using spherical caps.
  • When placed before a FAISS flat index, it improves query throughput by up to 382\% and by approximately 116\% on average across the five datasets, while returning the same range-search result.
  • Our results show that CapCover Filter can substantially improve vector-store throughput when similarity thresholds are tight, retrieval is expensive, and indexed embeddings are highly clustered.

[PP] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

TL;DR Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures increasingly consolidate operational relational metadata and high-dimensional vector embeddings within unified relational database management systems…

Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures increasingly consolidate operational relational metadata and high-dimensional vector embeddings within unified relational database management systems (RDBMSs) to eliminate cross-system synchronization latency and preserve transactional ACID guarantees. However, executing Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) searches—specifically over Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) proximity graphs and Inverted File with Flat Compression (IVFFlat) partitions—inside stateless, multi-tenant RAG microservices exposes a severe multi-objective optimization bottleneck. Production retrieval pipelines must simultaneously satisfy strict 99th-percentile (p99) tail-latency Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operate within bounded relational shared-buffer memory pools, and guarantee high top-k semantic recall (Recall@k) under non-stationary query concurrency.

entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives.

Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots.

entry.title: Authenticated Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Outsourced Vector Databases
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search has become a fundamental query primitive in modern vector databases for managing large-scale embedding data.

Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search has become a fundamental query primitive in modern vector databases for managing large-scale embedding data. To support growing vector collections, organizations increasingly outsource database management and query processing to third-party clouds. However, untrusted service providers may return suboptimal or fabricated results, posing a serious threat to ANN search integrity.

  • In this paper, we propose VIDA, a novel and efficient scheme for authenticated graph-based ANN search.
  • Furthermore, we introduce MeST, a topology-aware authenticated data structure that aligns authentication paths with graph traversal, significantly reducing structural proof overhead.
  • Additionally, we design a quantization-aware authentication strategy that exploits distance bounds for pruning, reducing the number of exact distances requiring cryptographic authentication.

Datasets: LAION, Cluster, For, Msmarco

entry.title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute.

Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute. Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact. We study early termination for such constrained $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) queries, with plain $k$-NN as a special case, and seek the cheapest stopping rule whose answer is exact with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$.

  • Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact.

Datasets: Amazon Reviews, Each

entry.title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Vector databases rely on Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) indexes for similarity search, but a graph built from data alone can be poorly matched to a skewed or changing query workload.

Vector databases rely on Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) indexes for similarity search, but a graph built from data alone can be poorly matched to a skewed or changing query workload. We present REWEAVE (Reward-Guided Rewiring of Vector Graphs), an online index-maintenance method that learns edge utility from query feedback and periodically rewires the bottom layer within the original per-node degree cap. The method supports sparse exact-neighbor feedback combined with self-labels, and standard HNSW serving without learning overhead once adaptation is disabled.

  • We present REWEAVE (Reward-Guided Rewiring of Vector Graphs), an online index-maintenance method that learns edge utility from query feedback and periodically rewires the bottom layer within the original per-node degree cap.
  • Under explicit assumptions we prove value-estimation and graph-stabilization guarantees.
  • Under stationary skew, REWEAVE improves held-out recall by up to 23.3 percentage points over HNSW.

Datasets: n/a

entry.title: Delaunay-Based Nearest Neighbor Search with Grid-Accelerated Queries and Parallel Construction
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Nearest-neighbor search is a fundamental primitive in computer graphics, with applications in distance field computation, surface reconstruction, and point cloud registration.

Nearest-neighbor search is a fundamental primitive in computer graphics, with applications in distance field computation, surface reconstruction, and point cloud registration. In many graphics applications, data points lie on a surface manifold embedded in 3D space, whereas queries are distributed throughout the surrounding volume, a setting in which spatial partitioning structures such as k-d trees and grids can become inefficient. Dynamic-programming-based nearest-neighbor search (DP-NNS) offers an alternative: it traverses a successor DAG that records the history of incremental Delaunay construction and often outperforms spatial partitioning structures.

  • Dynamic-programming-based nearest-neighbor search (DP-NNS) offers an alternative: it traverses a successor DAG that records the history of incremental Delaunay construction and often outperforms spatial partitioning structures.
  • For queries, we introduce a grid-based initialization strategy that precomputes valid starting points on the successor DAG, shortening search paths while preserving exactness and enabling a twofold speedup.
  • We further reorder query points to improve cache locality.

Datasets: Thingi10K, ABC, MedShapeNet, Augmented ICL-NUIM

entry.title: VecDBLens: An Evaluatology-Based Framework for Vector Database Diagnosis
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Vector databases are increasingly deployed as retrieval pipelines in which representation, indexing, and query-time execution jointly determine accuracy, throughput, and cost.

Vector databases are increasingly deployed as retrieval pipelines in which representation, indexing, and query-time execution jointly determine accuracy, throughput, and cost. Existing vector database evaluations primarily focus on indexing while treating embeddings as fixed inputs and ignoring the role of query-time execution, making it difficult to decide whether a bottleneck should be addressed by changing the embedding model, the index, or the query-processing functions. To address the above limitation, we introduce VecDBLens, an Evaluatology-based framework that treats the function under diagnosis as an evaluated object and all remaining dataset, workload, parameter, and runtime factors as matched evaluation conditions.

  • To address the above limitation, we introduce VecDBLens, an Evaluatology-based framework that treats the function under diagnosis as an evaluated object and all remaining dataset, workload, parameter, and runtime factors as matched evaluation conditions.
  • First, retrieval performance is fundamentally upper-bounded by embedding quality, revealing that many apparent indexing failures are therefore representation-side limitations.

Datasets: GIST1M

entry.title: HyperPage: Learned Page Layouts for Disk-Resident Graph Vector Indexes
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Disk-resident graph indexes such as DiskANN store each vector with its graph edges as one record on SSD pages.

Disk-resident graph indexes such as DiskANN store each vector with its graph edges as one record on SSD pages. A search needs the page of every record it expands, so its page reads depend on the page layout, that is, which records share a page. Search agents trained with reinforcement learning query one such index run after run, and every graph traversal can be logged with the records it expands.

  • Accordingly, we propose HyperPage, which first builds layouts for the declared budget on the logged traversals of uncached records.

entry.title: Function Inversion Reporting
entry.content:

entry.content:

TL;DR Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation.

Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor.

  • Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor.
  • Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance.

entry.title: Dynamic Graph Indexing for Label-Filtered Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entry.content:
[T1] SIGMOD 2027

TL;DR Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) over high-dimensional vectors is a core primitive in modern retrieval systems.

Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) over high-dimensional vectors is a core primitive in modern retrieval systems. In practice, objects are often also associated with labels (e.g., attributes or keywords), and retrieval must combine vector similarity with explicit label-based filtering, giving rise to label-filtered ANNS. This task is challenging because label filtering and ANNS favor very different index structures, selective filters fragment the admissible search space, and updates complicate index maintenance.

  • To address these challenges, we propose DYLAN, a dynamic composite index for label-filtered ANNS supporting containment, overlap, and their conjunctions and disjunctions.
  • Extensive experiments with real data show that DYLAN consistently improves query throughput at comparable recall, by up to two orders of magnitude on challenging label-rich datasets, while retaining competitive memory, construction, and update costs.

TL;DR Unlike the brain, artificial neural networks (ANNs) suffer from "catastrophic forgetting": complete overwriting of solutions when re-training on new functions ("concept shift") or on a disjoint domain of the current…

Unlike the brain, artificial neural networks (ANNs) suffer from "catastrophic forgetting": complete overwriting of solutions when re-training on new functions ("concept shift") or on a disjoint domain of the current function ("domain shift"). ANNs require each batch of data to be roughly representative of the complete distribution, a typically expensive and impractical requirement. In this paper, we introduce Functional Task Networks (FTNs), a method of continual learning and knowledge transfer modeled after several properties of the mammalian neocortex.

TL;DR Vector search runs as an operator in database systems, where a missed neighbor can make a filter, join, or aggregate wrong, yet approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes are tuned only for an average recall target.

Vector search runs as an operator in database systems, where a missed neighbor can make a filter, join, or aggregate wrong, yet approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes are tuned only for an average recall target. entry.title: Sharp Limits of Graph-Based Nearest Neighbor Search on the Sphere
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR We study the degree needed for greedy graph search to find the exact nearest neighbor from every starting point on graphs of $n$ independent data points on the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^d$.

We study the degree needed for greedy graph search to find the exact nearest neighbor from every starting point on graphs of $n$ independent data points on the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^d$. For uniform data, we determine an explicit sublinear degree threshold when $d$ is proportional to $\log n$, and the threshold $2^{d/2+o(d)}$ in the dense regime $\sqrt{\log n}\ll d\ll\log n$. Above these thresholds by fixed exponent gaps, the nearest-neighbor graph succeeds from every entry for most uniform queries with high probability, with evaluation cost on the same exponential scale as its degree.

entry.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods.

Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods. The fruit fly's olfactory circuit computes a locality-sensitive hash of sensory input using a strikingly different mechanism - sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition - and prior work (Dasgupta et al., 2017) showed this scheme, dubbed FlyHash, preserves neighbor structure better per bit than conventional random-hyperplane hashing (SimHash) on several benchmarks. We apply FlyHash, to our knowledge for the first time, to LLM agent memory retrieval, and ask three questions a practitioner actually needs answered: does the quality advantage hold under a correctly matched-bit protocol (it does, robustly, across 10 seeds and four datasets spanning two modalities, with one specific, previously undocumented comparison pitfall identified and corrected along the way); does that advantage translate into real memory and latency savings, including against the dense-vector indexing (HNSW) practitioners default to today (no: at equal bits FlyHash's codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash's, and HNSW dominates both hash methods at ordinary scale; a sparse-set comparison we introduce recovers most but not all of a naive latency gap, leaving hashing's practical case narrower and more specific than the quality result alone implies); and does the advantage survive genuine, non-circular agent-memory relevance labels rather than the nearest-neighbor-by-embedding proxy this literature otherwise relies on (it does).

Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search over neural embeddings powers modern retrieval systems such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Embeddings come in three representations (dense, sparse and multi-vector), and efficient search combines an index structure, a similarity function and a quantization scheme. Existing libraries fix one combination, hard-code each one separately, or factor only one side of the problem, and none covers all three representations.

entry.title: O2N2: Efficient Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring.

Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring. Among the various privacy-preserving primitives, trusted execution environments (TEEs) have much lower overhead than heavy cryptographic ones, yet they leak memory access patterns, enabling adversaries to infer query contents. Oblivious RAM (ORAM) can be used to hide those access patterns at $\mathrm{O}(\log N)$ asymptotic cost, but existing high-performance ANN search algorithms (e.g., IVF or HNSW) exhibit complex, data-dependent access patterns that are unfriendly for ORAM.

  • We introduce O2N2, a doubly oblivious ANN framework built around single-path search in randomly rotated $k$-d tree forests.

Datasets: Given

entry.content:

TL;DR Vector databases are now core infrastructure for AI retrieval systems, yet many real deployments must serve queries over multiple independently constructed vectorDBs built with different embedding models.

Vector databases are now core infrastructure for AI retrieval systems, yet many real deployments must serve queries over multiple independently constructed vectorDBs built with different embedding models. This creates a systems problem of federated retrieval over heterogeneous vectorDBs: vectors and similarity scores are not directly comparable across embedding spaces, while fully resolving this incompatibility through corpus-wide re-embedding and re-indexing is often operationally prohibitive. Existing methods therefore face a difficult trade-off between retrieval quality, construction cost, and query throughput.

  • We present HVMap, a lightweight compatibility layer for federated retrieval across heterogeneous vectorDBs.

Large-scale ANNS systems often exploit storage in addition to DRAM for supporting vector search. entry.content:

Approximate nearest-neighbor search on GPUs serves retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation, and deduplication over datasets of up to billions of vectors. The fastest GPU indexes at high recall, such as CAGRA, walk proximity graphs in chained rounds, each of which waits for the distances of the previous one. entry.title: The Tangled Web They Weave: Exploring Neural Representations with Directed Simplicial Complexes
entry.content:
[PP] arXiv preprint

TL;DR Understanding how artificial neural networks (ANNs) represent and combine features internally is a central challenge in mechanistic interpretability.

Understanding how artificial neural networks (ANNs) represent and combine features internally is a central challenge in mechanistic interpretability. Existing neural circuit-discovery methods represent neuron interactions as pairwise edges in a graph. But distributed neural representations consist of large groups of neurons that are inherently linked by higher-order causal dependencies: suppressing a subgroup of neurons in concert may shift the activation of other neurons in the feature representation.

  • We propose a method to construct filtered directed simplicial complexes (DSCs) that give a topological representation of such dependencies, built from the activation profiles of an ANN on a given set of inputs.
  • Our approach treats ANNs as structural causal models and uses counterfactual ablations to test for causal links between groups of internal neurons within specific input contexts.
  • As validation, we compare our method with graph-based circuit-discovery baselines and find that their 1-skeletons agree within the relations that a weight graph can represent.

entry.content:

TL;DR Vector search has become a database operator with many physical implementations: different index families, build-time and search-time parameters, and compressed or disk-resident variants.

Vector search has become a database operator with many physical implementations: different index families, build-time and search-time parameters, and compressed or disk-resident variants. Each trades cost against fidelity, the fraction of a query's exact top-k nearest neighbors that a configuration returns. Deployments nevertheless choose one configuration offline and use it for every query, so they are sized for their hardest queries and overpay for the rest.
